explainBack.question: Why does drawing a rough sketch or placing a comment on an image work better than writing a longer, more detailed prompt?
explainBack.answer: Because a sketch carries spatial information directly — relative positions, sizes and empty space — that prose describes ambiguously, and a comment pins the edit to one region so the system regenerates only what you targeted while keeping the rest. A longer prompt forces every constraint through words, where the model must reconstruct your layout from description; the visual input hands it the layout ready-made. Crucially, the system still generates a new image each time, so precise text, measurements and brand details must be verified outside the picture.
explainBack.expectedEvidence: P005 (visual communication versus one long prompt), P006 (sketch as rough map, comment as smaller editing target, new-image limit), P010 (better context routes beat longer prompts).
explainBack.assessment: The article's mechanism fully supports this causal answer in ordinary language; the limit on editability survives the explanation, so explain-back passes.

unseenTransfer.scenario: A school administrator must produce a bilingual open-day flyer: the school crest top-left, a map snippet bottom-right, and event times in a centre column. Her first attempt used a 200-word prompt and the tool kept swapping the crest and map positions; she also notices the printed times sometimes come out wrong.
unseenTransfer.question: Using this article's mechanism, how should she guide the tool, and what should she never trust the generated image to get right?
unseenTransfer.answer: She should sketch the flyer's three zones — crest box top-left, map box bottom-right, centre column — so the spatial layout arrives as visual context rather than ambiguous prose, then add only the few must-keep details in words. If one region is wrong, she should place a comment on that region for a targeted regeneration instead of rewriting the whole prompt. Because the output is a generated image, not a design file with live text, she must verify the event times, translations and crest fidelity outside the picture — ideally having a designer rebuild final text — since factual copy inside a generated image is exactly what the article warns still needs external checking.
unseenTransfer.expectedEvidence: The reasoning applies P006 (map/target mechanism and new-image limit), P007 (copy and factual details checked outside the picture) and P010 (prefer a better context route over a longer prompt) to a situation absent from the article.
unseenTransfer.assessment: The mechanism transfers cleanly and completely to this new scenario, including its limits, so transfer passes.
